candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential; monitor clients with invasive devices and interpret physiologic monitoring data to reduce treatment-related risk
candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — arterial-line monitoring and prevention of arterial medication administration
candidate.educational_objective: Use an arterial catheter for continuous blood-pressure monitoring during tightly titrated vasoactive therapy while preventing the serious safety error of administering medication through the arterial line.

options.A: The arterial catheter can provide continuous beat-to-beat blood-pressure data for precise titration, but the antihypertensive medication should not be infused through the arterial line.
options.B: The arterial catheter should be used as the preferred route for the antihypertensive infusion because arterial delivery improves blood-pressure control.
options.C: The arterial catheter replaces the need to assess the client for organ perfusion or other hemodynamic changes.
options.D: The arterial catheter measures glucose continuously and therefore has little role in titrating vasoactive medication.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current NCBI/StatPearls guidance describes arterial catheterization as a method for continuous systolic, diastolic, and mean arterial pressure monitoring, which is particularly useful when vasoactive medications require precise titration. The same guidance explicitly states that medication administration through an arterial line must be avoided because serious ischemic and limb-threatening complications can occur. Hypertensive-emergency guidance also supports continuous hemodynamic monitoring during titratable IV therapy. B is dangerous because an arterial catheter is not a medication-infusion route. C overstates what one monitoring device can replace, and D misidentifies the variable being measured.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Arterial catheters provide continuous real-time blood-pressure monitoring that can support precise vasoactive titration, but medications must not be administered through arterial lines because of serious injury risk.
candidate.source_locator: Arterial Lines — continuous systolic/diastolic/MAP monitoring through a transducer; real-time monitoring supports precise titration of vasoactive medications; medication administration through arterial lines must be strictly avoided because of severe complications. Hypertensive Crisis — IV antihypertensives administered with continuous hemodynamic monitoring; arterial catheterization may be considered for precise beat-to-beat monitoring when tightly controlled BP adjustment is required
